note: Hebrew ha'almah is "the young woman" (of marriageable age; the specific word for virgin is betulah), and harah is an adjective, "pregnant" (now or about to be). The KJV follows the LXX parthenos, the reading Matthew 1:23 quotes. Theologically the most debated verse in Isaiah. Context: the young woman is pregnant (a sign in Ahaz's own time) (high confidence). 7:15-16 'before the boy knows how to refuse evil ... the land whose two kings you dread will be deserted' sets the sign within a few years; 8:3-4 gives a parallel birth-sign. Matthew's later use of the Greek text is a separate matter.

kjv: that he may know to refuse the evil
mine: when he knows how to refuse the evil
note: Hebrew leda'to is temporal ("by the time he knows"), dating the sign by the child's age (cf. v. 16), not giving the purpose of his diet.
